methods.name: Push
methods.description:
Push an evals/ folder as an eval's new version.
 Creates the eval if the organization has none with the slug, or adds a
 version to the one it has; pushing the folder the eval already holds
 changes nothing, and with a new tag only moves the tag. The response's
 status lists the cases and what could not be read.

 Error Cases:

 - INVALID_ARGUMENT: the archive is not a ZIP within the limits, or no
   case in it loads; the error lists the problems
 - FAILED_PRECONDITION: the slug was renamed away from (SLUG_RENAMED)
 - PERMISSION_DENIED: the caller may not create evals in the
   organization, or may not edit the eval with this slug

methods.name: AddCaseFromRun
methods.description:
Add a case built from a run (as buildCaseFromRun builds it) to an
 eval, as a new version holding the current version's files and the
 case.

 Error Cases:

 - NOT_FOUND: no such run, or no such eval
 - PERMISSION_DENIED: the caller may not view the run, or may not edit
   the eval
 - FAILED_PRECONDITION: the run has not ended, or the eval is not of the
   run's organization
 - ALREADY_EXISTS: the eval already holds a case of that name

methods.name: CreateArtifactUploadUrl
methods.description:
Mint a short-lived, single-use upload URL for staging an eval archive
 that exceeds the gRPC message-size cap (10MB). Flow:

 1. createArtifactUploadUrl(org, slug, size_bytes) → { url, artifact_upload_ref }
 2. HTTP PUT the ZIP bytes to url
 3. push(PushEvalRequest{ slug, artifact_upload_ref })

methods.name: UpdateVisibility
methods.description:
Update the visibility of an eval: the whole organization, or its owner
 alone. Only modifies metadata.visibility.

methods.name: Rename
methods.description:
Rename an eval: change its slug.

 The eval keeps its id, its versions and its grants, and every answer
 names it by the new slug. The old slug keeps leading to the eval for
 reading for 30 days, during which no other eval of the organization can
 take it and this one can take it back; then it is released. A push that
 names the old slug is refused with SLUG_RENAMED. A slug another eval
 holds is refused with ALREADY_EXISTS, and one another eval was recently
 renamed away from with SLUG_RESERVED.

methods.name: Delete
methods.description: Delete an eval and every version of it.

methods.name: Get
methods.description: Get a single eval by ID.

methods.name: GetByReference
methods.description:
Get an eval by API resource reference, at a version.

 Version resolution (via ApiResourceReference.version field):
 - Empty/"latest" → Returns the current version
 - Tag name (e.g. "stable") → Resolves to the version holding this tag
 - SHA-256 digest (64 hex chars) → Returns the exact immutable version

methods.name: List
methods.description:
List an organization's evals, newest first.

 Returns the evals of the input org that the caller may view, one page at
 a time.

methods.name: ListVersions
methods.description:
List an eval's versions, newest first, each with its digest, tag,
 message and who pushed it.

methods.name: Download
methods.description:
Download one version of an eval as the ZIP archive it was pushed as.
 The reference's version picks it as getByReference does; none is the
 current version. Larger archives ride getDownloadUrl.

methods.name: GetDownloadUrl
methods.description:
Mint a URL for downloading one version of an eval over HTTP.

 Preferred over download for anything that might exceed the gRPC
 message-size cap (10MB). The reference's version picks the version as
 getByReference does.

methods.name: BuildCaseFromRun
methods.description:
Build an eval case from a run, to keep on disk or push in an eval.

 The case is the turn the run answered: its request as the prompt, the
 conversation before it as the case's history (so the case resumes where
 the person was), each MCP tool answer the run got as a fixed mock under
 the server name the turn gave it, and a rubric to fill in, seeded with
 why the run went wrong (an AI judge's failing reason, or the caller's
 own thumbs-down note). It never carries a verdict of its own.

 Error Cases:

 - NOT_FOUND: no such run
 - PERMISSION_DENIED: the caller may not view the run
 - FAILED_PRECONDITION: the run has not ended
 - RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: the case is too large to answer inline; add it
   to an eval with addCaseFromRun, which writes it on the server

methodTypes.name: PushEvalRequest
methodTypes.description:
PushEvalRequest stores an evals/ folder as an eval's new version.
 Creates the eval if no eval of the organization has the slug, or adds a
 version to the one that has it; pushing the folder the eval already holds
 changes nothing.

 The folder travels as a ZIP archive, one of two ways (exactly one must
 be set):
 - artifact: inline ZIP bytes, bounded by the gRPC message-size cap (10MB).
 - artifact_upload_ref: a reference to bytes staged via
   createArtifactUploadUrl() + HTTP PUT, for archives above the cap.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization the eval belongs to.

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
The eval's slug, unique within the organization: the eval this push
 creates or adds a version to.

 A slug an eval of the organization was renamed away from in the last 30
 days is refused with SLUG_RENAMED: push to its new slug.

fields.name: Name
fields.description:
The eval's display name. Empty keeps the stored one, or is the slug when
 the push creates the eval.

fields.name: Artifact
fields.description:
The folder as a ZIP archive, its case directories, mocks/ and any
 shared files at the archive root.

 Mutually exclusive with artifact_upload_ref (see the message comment).

fields.name: ArtifactUploadRef
fields.description:
Reference to an archive staged via createArtifactUploadUrl().

 Mutually exclusive with artifact (see the message comment).

fields.name: Visibility
fields.description:
Visibility for the eval: the whole organization or its owner alone.
 Unspecified keeps the stored level, or is the organization when the push
 creates the eval.

fields.name: Message
fields.description:
Optional human-readable message describing this version, such as the
 commit it was pushed from, kept in metadata.version.message for the
 version history.

fields.name: Tag
fields.description:
Optional tag to move to this version, such as "stable". A push with a
 tag onto the folder the eval already holds moves the tag and adds no
 version. "latest" is refused: it always names the current version.

methodTypes.name: AddEvalCaseFromRunRequest
methodTypes.description:
AddEvalCaseFromRunRequest asks for a run's turn built as a case (as
 buildCaseFromRun builds it) and added to an eval as a new version.

fields.name: RunId
fields.description: The run whose turn becomes the case. It must have ended.

fields.name: Eval
fields.description:
The eval to add the case to, by slug or id; its organization must be
 the run's. Its version is ignored: the case joins the current one.

fields.name: CaseName
fields.description:
The case's directory name. Empty suggests one from the request. A name
 the eval already holds is refused.

fields.name: Skill
fields.description: A skill the run should have read and did not, as "<plugin>:<skill>".

fields.name: Message
fields.description: The new version's message. Empty is "case <name> from run <id>".

fields.name: Tag
fields.description: Optional tag to move to the new version. "latest" is refused.

methodTypes.name: CreateEvalArtifactUploadUrlRequest
methodTypes.description:
CreateEvalArtifactUploadUrlRequest asks the server to mint a staging
 slot for an eval archive too large to travel inline.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization the eval belongs to.

fields.name: Slug
fields.description: The slug the push will name: minting asks exactly what that push asks.

fields.name: SizeBytes
fields.description:
Declared size of the archive in bytes; an over-limit declaration is
 refused before any bytes move.

methodTypes.name: EvalArtifactUploadUrl
methodTypes.description:
EvalArtifactUploadUrl is a short-lived, single-use capability for staging
 an eval archive over HTTP.

fields.name: Url
fields.description: URL to PUT the archive bytes to. Content-Type: application/zip.

fields.name: ArtifactUploadRef
fields.description:
Opaque reference to pass as PushEvalRequest.artifact_upload_ref after
 the PUT succeeds. Single-use; invalid after the push consumes it or the
 TTL lapses.

fields.name: TtlSeconds
fields.description: Time-to-live for the upload URL in seconds.

methodTypes.name: UpdateVisibilityInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for updating the visibility of any API resource.

 Used by resource-specific command controllers to change visibility.
 Each controller's updateVisibility RPC accepts this shared input
 and returns the full updated resource.

 Visibility transitions trigger FGA tuple management in Cloud mode. Each
 level maps to exactly one tuple shape; on a transition the tuple for the
 old level is removed and the tuple for the new level is created:
 - PRIVATE:  no visibility tuple (owner + explicit grants only)
 - ORG:      resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

 Not all resources support all visibility levels — the supported set is
 declared per kind via VisibilityConfig in kind_meta:
 - Blueprints (agent, skill, plugin):
     PRIVATE, ORG, or CHILD_ORGS
 - Org-only kinds (vault):
     PRIVATE or ORG (never CHILD_ORGS — tenant isolation)

 visibility_public is refused for every kind (INVALID_ARGUMENT naming the
 supported levels); the level is retired.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: ID of the resource whose visibility is being updated.

fields.name: Visibility
fields.description:
The new visibility setting for the resource.
 Must not be unspecified (0). Valid values depend on resource kind —
 see the VisibilityConfig in the kind's kind_meta.

methodTypes.name: RenameInput
methodTypes.description:
Input for renaming any API resource: changing its slug.

 Used by resource-specific command controllers whose kind lets a slug
 change. Each controller's rename RPC accepts this shared input and returns
 the full updated resource. A resource's slug never changes through update
 or apply; rename is its only writer.

fields.name: ResourceId
fields.description: ID of the resource being renamed.

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
The new slug. Same format as metadata.slug, at most 63 characters: the
 longest a reference's org takes.

methodTypes.name: ApiResourceReference
methodTypes.description:
Generic reference to any API resource.
 Used across resources to reference other resources (e.g., Vault, Agent, Skill).
 Canonical written format: "org/slug" (e.g., "acme/web-search", "acme/my-agent").

 A reference has three forms:
 - Written: by name (org and slug), by id, or by both. A write that carries
   both must have them agree, or it is refused naming both. A name is
   resolved to its resource's id when the referring resource is written.
 - Stored: org (the organization's id), kind, id and version. The slug is
   not stored, so a reference keeps pointing at the resource it meant when
   that resource is renamed, and never at a new resource that takes its old
   name after it is deleted.
 - Returned: as stored, with slug filled with the resource's current name.
   A reference whose resource was deleted is returned with an empty slug.

 The kind a reference names is the kind its field declares
 (reference_kind); a reference that carries another kind is refused.

 Every reference in a resource's spec is checked when the resource is
 written: the target must exist, and a target in another organization
 must be one the writing organization's parent shares with its child
 organizations (visibility_child_orgs) to be referenced at all. A blueprint may not be
 more visible than the skills, plugins and agents it references, so
 what a person can run they can also read. A reference that fails the
 check is refused at write, never at run.

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization that owns the referenced resource, by slug or id.

 When non-empty: an organization slug (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens,
 starts with a letter, 2-63 characters; e.g. "stigmer", "acme-corp") or an
 organization id (org_<ulid>). The server stores the id, so a stored
 reference keeps pointing at its organization across a rename.

 When empty: the reference is relative — the server resolves it to the parent
 resource's organization at write time. All stored and returned references
 always have org populated (absolute form, the id).

 Use empty org for same-org references (the common case).
 An explicit other org is accepted only when that organization is your
 organization's parent and shares the resource with its children
 (visibility_child_orgs).

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Kind of the referenced resource (e.g., SKILL, AGENT, PLUGIN).

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
Resource slug (user-friendly identifier, unique within org).
 Format: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must start with a letter
 and end with a letter or digit (e.g., "web-search", "code-reviewer").
 Length: 2-63 characters.

 Written to name the resource; never stored; returned filled with the
 resource's current name, empty when the resource was deleted.

fields.name: Version
fields.description:
The version of a skill, a plugin or a subagent the reference asks for;
 every other kind ignores it.

 Formats:
 - empty or "latest": the latest version;
 - a tag (e.g. "stable", "v1.0"): the version the tag names;
 - a 64-character hash: that exact version, which never changes.

 When it is read: a skill or plugin reference is resolved at the start
 of each turn, so a reference without a hash follows each new push, and
 the run records the version it loaded (RunStatus.loaded_versions). A
 subagent reference is resolved once, when the agent that lists it is
 saved, and the saved reference carries the hash it resolved to.

fields.name: Id
fields.description:
The referenced resource's id: what a stored reference holds. Optional
 on write, where the slug may name the resource instead; an id no
 resource of the kind holds answers as a missing resource. At most 64
 characters.

methodTypes.name: ListEvalsRequest
methodTypes.description: Input for listing an organization's evals, newest first.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization whose evals to list, by id or slug.

fields.name: PageSize
fields.description:
The most entries to return: 0 asks for the default page of 50, and a
 size above 100 is read as 100.

fields.name: PageToken
fields.description:
The previous response's next_page_token, to continue that list; every
 other field must equal that request's, or the call is refused.

fields.name: Labels
fields.description:
Only resources carrying every label given, each matched exactly (AND).
 A selective filter may answer short pages, even empty ones, that still
 carry a token.

methodTypes.name: EvalList
methodTypes.description: One page of an organization's evals.

fields.name: Entries
fields.description: The evals in this page, newest first.

fields.name: NextPageToken
fields.description:
Set when more entries may follow: pass it as page_token to continue.
 A page may be short, even empty, and still carry a token.

methodTypes.name: ListEvalVersionsInput
methodTypes.description: ListEvalVersionsInput requests the version history of an eval.

fields.name: Org
fields.description: Organization that owns the eval.

fields.name: Slug
fields.description: Eval slug (unique within the organization).

fields.name: PageToken
fields.description:
The previous response's next_page_token, to continue that list; every
 other field must equal that request's, or the call is refused.

fields.name: PageSize
fields.description:
The most entries to return: 0 asks for the default page of 50, and a
 size above 100 is read as 100.

methodTypes.name: ListEvalVersionsResponse
methodTypes.description: ListEvalVersionsResponse is a page of an eval's version history.

fields.name: Entries
fields.description: Versions, newest first.

fields.name: NextPageToken
fields.description:
Set when more entries may follow: pass it as page_token to continue.
 A page may be short, even empty, and still carry a token.

methodTypes.name: EvalArchive
methodTypes.description:
EvalArchive is one version of an eval as the ZIP archive it was pushed
 as.

fields.name: Artifact
fields.description: The archive bytes.

fields.name: Digest
fields.description: SHA-256 of the archive: the version's digest.

methodTypes.name: EvalArchiveDownloadUrl
methodTypes.description:
EvalArchiveDownloadUrl is a URL to download one version of an eval over
 HTTP.

fields.name: Url
fields.description: URL to download the archive ZIP via HTTP GET.

fields.name: TtlSeconds
fields.description: Time-to-live for the download URL in seconds; 0 means no expiry.

fields.name: SizeBytes
fields.description: Size of the archive ZIP in bytes.

fields.name: Digest
fields.description:
SHA-256 of the archive: the version's digest, which the downloaded
 bytes must match.

methodTypes.name: BuildEvalCaseFromRunRequest
methodTypes.description:
BuildEvalCaseFromRunRequest asks for one eval case built from a run: the
 turn the run answered, the conversation before it, the tool answers it
 got and a rubric to fill in.

fields.name: RunId
fields.description: The run whose turn becomes the case. It must have ended.

fields.name: CaseName
fields.description: The case's directory name. Empty suggests one from the request.

fields.name: Skill
fields.description:
A skill the run should have read and did not, as "<plugin>:<skill>":
 the case gains a check that the skill is read. Empty adds none.

methodTypes.name: EvalCaseArchive
methodTypes.description:
EvalCaseArchive is one eval case folder as a ZIP archive: the case's
 directory at the archive's root, in the order `stigmer push eval` writes
 it.

fields.name: CaseName
fields.description: The case's directory name, the archive's one top-level directory.

fields.name: Artifact
fields.description: The archive bytes.

fields.name: Digest
fields.description: SHA-256 of the archive.

fields.name: Notes
fields.description:
What the case leaves out or keeps differently from the run, one
 sentence each: a tool answered differently on a later call, a platform
 tool no mock stands in for, an attachment, a tool use the conversation
 never answered. Empty when the case is the run's turn whole.

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines which
 users, inside that organization or in its child organizations, can read
 the resource. No level reaches every
 account on the server.

 The visibility levels map to FGA tuples:
 - PRIVATE: no additional viewer tuples (owner-only access)
 - ORG: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer tuple (everyone in the
   org — the org role hierarchy flows downward, so owners, admins, members
   AND read-only viewers all satisfy the organization#viewer userset)
 - CHILD_ORGS: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer
   (everyone in every child organization of the owning organization)
 - PUBLIC: retired; see the value's own comment.

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only the owner, explicitly granted principals, and — for blueprint kinds
 in the cloud edition — org admins can access.
 This is the default for personal and run-scoped resources.

 Org admins count as owners of blueprint kinds (agent, channel,
 skill, plugin), so a private blueprint stays
 manageable — and visible — to its org's admins. Personal kinds
 (sessions) stay creator-only.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Retired. This level made a resource readable to every account on the
 server; it is refused at create and at updateVisibility for every kind,
 and every stored row that held it has been moved to visibility_org.
 Sharing across organizations happens through plugins (a copy is
 installed and owned) or, from a parent organization to its children,
 through visibility_child_orgs.

values.name: visibility_org
values.description:
Everyone in the owning organization can access (read) this resource —
 all org roles including read-only viewers (the role just-in-time provisioning
 grants by default). Running or otherwise spending against the resource
 still requires the org-level member-or-guest permissions
 (can_create_session / can_create_run_in); org visibility widens
 read, never spend.

 FGA tuple: resource#viewer@organization:<org>#viewer
 (The tuple once targeted organization#member, which
 excluded viewer-role users; the authorization model no longer admits
 that shape.)

values.name: visibility_child_orgs
values.description:
Everyone in every child organization of the owning organization can
 read and run this resource: the shared catalog an organization offers
 the organizations under it (spec.parent_org). Child organizations
 created later gain access automatically, and no other organization
 does. Instances, sessions, runs and vaults are never shared
 this way: each child runs the shared blueprint inside its own boundary.

 Only valid for blueprint kinds with supports_child_orgs: true, and only
 in an organization that is not itself a child.

 FGA tuple: resource#child_org_viewer@organization:<org>#child_org_viewer

values.name: api_resource_version
values.description: Immutable version record tracking changes to an API resource.

values.name: grant
values.description:
One role given to one principal on one resource. Who holds what on a
 resource is the set of its grants.

values.name: identity_account
values.description: User account in the identity system.

values.name: api_key
values.description: Credential for programmatic API access.

values.name: invitation
values.description: Shareable link for joining an organization with a configurable role.

values.name: federation_issuer
values.description:
An outside issuer whose tokens Stigmer accepts for its own users
 (identity federation): its keys, its audience, and what its tokens get.

values.name: oauth_app
values.description: Registered OAuth application with an external vendor for outbound authentication.

values.name: team
values.description: Named group of an organization's people that access is shared with as one.

values.name: organization
values.description:
The boundary that holds people, Agents, Sessions and secrets
 together; nothing outside it sees them.

 Its id is a minted org_<ulid> that never changes; every organization-scoped
 resource names it by that id (metadata.org). Its slug is unique across the
 server and may change through rename; requests may name the organization
 by either.

values.name: platform
values.description: Singleton platform instance representing the Stigmer deployment.

values.name: agent
values.description: AI assistant with instructions, tools, skills, and a delegation model.

values.name: run
values.description: Single run of an agent within a session, tracking tool calls and responses.

values.name: session
values.description: Conversation thread between a user and an agent.

values.name: skill
values.description: Knowledge resource that provides domain-specific context to an agent.

values.name: channel
values.description:
A way people reach an agent: a chat link or website widget, a Slack
 workspace, or a WhatsApp number.

values.name: channel_app
values.description:
Customer-owned messaging-platform app (e.g. a Slack app) that
 channels can install through instead of the shared platform app.

values.name: schedule
values.description: Recurring trigger that runs an agent on a cron schedule.

values.name: memory
values.description: Agent-proposed, user-confirmed fact the platform remembers about a person.

values.name: plugin
values.description:
An installed Agent Plugins package: one thing holding skills, agents,
 hooks and MCP servers, which agents and conversations list whole.

values.name: vault
values.description:
A person's or an organization's box of logins (matched by a tool's
 address) and secrets (matched by name) that runs use.

values.name: score
values.description:
One grade of a finished run: a person's thumbs or a free run-health
 check.

values.name: scoring_rule
values.description:
AI grading switched on for one agent: its sample rate, monthly spending
 limit and judge model.

values.name: eval_run
values.description:
One run of test cases on an agent, or on a plugin on the built-in
 assistant, optionally with and without a plugin.

values.name: eval
values.description:
A set of test cases for an agent: an evals/ folder in Claude Code's
 plugin-eval format, pushed whole.

values.name: plan
values.description:
Catalog entry naming a bundle of entitlements and the terms that buy it.

 Platform-level: a plan belongs to no organization, so it carries no
 authorization scope and no owner. Immutable once created; a change of
 terms is a new Plan and the old one retires.

values.name: subscription
values.description:
An organization's binding to a Plan; at most one active per organization.

 System-created: the payment system drives its lifecycle, so it has no
 owner and grants no roles. Its reads and writes authorize on the
 organization through the billing permissions.

values.name: license
values.description:
A signed grant of entitlements to a self-hosting customer for a term.

 Platform-level: issued by the cloud's operators and verified offline by
 the Enterprise server, so the customer is a value inside the license
 (which may or may not name a cloud organization) and the kind has no
 authorization scope and no owner. Claims are immutable once signed; a
 renewal is a new License.

resourceDescription:
Eval is a set of test cases for an agent: an evals/ folder in Claude
 Code's plugin-eval format, pushed whole and kept with every version.

 Each case is a request a user might type, plus checks such as "the reply
 mentions the renamed function" or a pass-or-fail rubric for an AI judge.
 Pushing the same folder again changes nothing; a changed folder is a new
 version, reachable by its digest or by a tag.

statusType.name: EvalStatus
statusType.description:
EvalStatus is what an eval's current version holds: its digest and its
 test cases, read when it was pushed.

fields.name: Audit
fields.description: Standard audit information tracking creation and modification.

fields.name: Digest
fields.description:
SHA-256 of the pushed folder's archive, the immutable version
 identifier.

fields.name: CaseCount
fields.description: Cases in the folder, listed or not.

fields.name: CaseTags
fields.description: The tags the listed cases carry, once each, sorted: at most 200.

fields.name: Cases
fields.description: Each case, in directory order: at most 200.

fields.name: Findings
fields.description:
Problems reading the folder: a case that cannot load, an unknown field,
 a mock directory whose name no MCP server could have. At most 50.

fields.name: MockServers
fields.description:
The MCP servers the folder's mocks stand in for, by the directory names
 under mocks/, sorted.

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAudit
statusNestedTypes.description: ApiResourceAudit contains both spec-level and status-level audit details.

fields.name: SpecAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's specification (desired state).

fields.name: StatusAudit
fields.description: Audit info for the resource's status (actual state).

statusNestedTypes.name: ApiResourceAuditActor
statusNestedTypes.description:
ApiResourceAuditActor represents the entity that performed an action.

 This is the platform's single actor vocabulary: every "who did this"
 reference (created_by / updated_by, version-history applied_by / pushed_by,
 approval resolved_by_actor) uses this message, so actor rendering is
 uniform across all surfaces.

fields.name: Id
fields.description: Unique identifier of the actor.

fields.name: Avatar
fields.description: URL to the actor's avatar image.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.description:
Human-readable display name (e.g. "Ada Lovelace"). Empty when unknown;
 renderers fall back to email, then id.

fields.name: Email
fields.description:
Email address of the actor. Empty when unknown or not applicable
 (e.g. machine accounts).

fields.name: MintedBy
fields.description:
The service account whose key minted the user token the actor acted
 through. Empty for every other credential, and on an actor that records
 no act (an account's profile lookup).

fields.name: CreatedBy
fields.description: Actor who created this resource.

fields.name: CreatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was created.

fields.name: UpdatedBy
fields.description: Actor who last updated this resource.

fields.name: UpdatedAt
fields.description: Timestamp when the resource was last updated.

fields.name: Event
fields.description: Type of the last event (e.g., "created", "updated").

statusNestedTypes.name: EvalCaseSummary
statusNestedTypes.description: EvalCaseSummary is one test case of an eval.

fields.name: CaseName
fields.description: The case's name.

fields.name: Path
fields.description: The case's directory, relative to the folder's root.

fields.name: CaseTags
fields.description: The case's tags.

fields.name: Unsupported
fields.description:
Why Stigmer cannot run the case yet, naming the feature, as in
 "plugins" for a case that runs with a plugin; empty when it can.

statusNestedTypes.name: EvalFinding
statusNestedTypes.description:
EvalFinding is one problem a push found reading an eval's folder and did
 not refuse.

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Stable finding kind, e.g. "eval-case-invalid", "eval-mock-invalid".

fields.name: Message
fields.description: The finding as one user-facing sentence.

fields.name: Path
fields.description: The folder-relative path the finding points at.
